parsed.main_gap: Pigeonhole in Section 5 is miscounted: 2^{n+1}-3 gaps summing to <1 only give a gap <1/(2^{n+1}-3), not ≤1/(2^{n+1}-1); needs all 2^{n+1} subsets including ∅ and the full set.

errors.description: Claim (11) about nonempty proper subsets is false as stated (e.g. n=1, lengths 0.1 and 0.9: the two proper subset sums differ by 0.8 > 1/3). The correct argument uses all 2^{n+1} subset sums in [0,1] (including 0 and 1), whose 2^{n+1}-1 gaps sum to exactly 1. The write-up's subsequent case analysis (one of A,B empty) already handles the resulting cases, so the repair is a one-line fix.
errors.quote:
They lie in $(0,1)$, so their $2^{n+1}-3$ consecutive gaps sum to less than $1$. When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most
\[
\frac1{2^{n+1}-1}=d. \tag{11}
\]

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) correct. Claiming-stage value D, pairing characterization, common-refinement cut count, and the tree-component/signed-powers-of-two lower bound are all correct and carefully justified. Only flaw is the miscounted pigeonhole (false intermediate claim), trivially repairable and structurally anticipated by the empty-case handling.
